newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Redland in sale talks for French unit.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Redland in sale talks for French unit.

text.p: British building materials group Redland Plc said on Thursday it had put its French aggregates business up for sale in a bid to improve shareholder value after bad weather, sluggish European markets and a strong pound hit its1996 results.

Redland chief executive Robert Napier told Reuters the company was in "in active discussions with a number of interested parties" on the sale of its loss-making French unit Granulats, which has a book value of 310 million pounds ($504.8 million).
News of the planned disposal was welcomed by the market and Redland shares soared 19 pence to 372.5p before edging back to 361.5 by late morning.

"The French operations were always something of a problem and it's positive news that they're getting rid of them. That's been the real good news today," said one market-maker. Granulats, with 2,500 employees, has suffered from cuts and delays in public spending on infrastructure projects. Volume falls and price pressures in ready-mixed concrete resulted in an eight million pound loss.
This led Redland's 1996 profits to fall to 259.1 million pounds, before exceptionals, down from 273.2 million in 1995.

After accounting for a one-off hit of 58 million pounds to account for goodwill related to the purchase of its Steetley subsidiary in 1992, Redland's profits fell to 200.9 million. Sales dropped to 2.37 billion versus 2.50 billion, with the year dividend frozen at 16.67 pence per share.

The profit fallback, despite a strong U.S. aggregates performance, was blamed on bad weather in Europe last winter, sluggish German and French markets and the strong pound, which knocked seven million pounds off operating profits in 1996.
Napier said that if sterling remained at current levels through 1997 profts could suffer by 25 million pounds.
The group had said in its results statement earlier that it was "reviewing the strategic options" for the business, but disclosed in the interview it was already in talks with buyers.

This followed intense speculation over recent months that Redland was planning to spin off part or all its aggregates business. But the company remains committed to retaining its successful U.S. aggregates arm alongside the main European Roofing business RBB.
"The sale of the French aggregates leaves us with the European roofing division and a strong and successful U.S. aggregates division plus an improving UK business," Napier said.
Commenting on the outlook for the RBB roofing business in Germany, he said building permit numbers have stabilised.
"So in 1997 we should see a flat or only slightly declining market."
Price rises, plus lower variable costs meant "overall the Deutsche mark profits will be at least the same in 1997 despite a fall in volumes."
The group plans to expand its RBB operations in eastern Europe and said regional sales should rise 20 percent this year after 25 percent East European growth in 1996.
It also plans to spend $40-50 million on bolt-on acquisitions in the U.S. aggregates business, Napier said. ($ = 0.614 British Pounds)
